comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C5. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the FMNL2 expression and localization data supported by converging evidence from western blotting, fluorescence microscopy, and co-staining experiments across species.

Disagreement on claims C6-C11. OpenEval finds the FMNL2 knockdown and polar body extrusion defects well-supported with appropriate rescue experiments. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting reliance on a single knockdown approach (siRNA) and recommending additional methods (Trim-Away or morpholino) to confirm specificity and rule out off-target effects.

Disagreement on claims C12-C17. OpenEval finds spindle migration defects well-supported by time-lapse imaging, L/D ratio quantification, and rescue experiments. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the quantification methodology, noting that distance measurements would be more accurate than contact assessment, and that representative images lack spindle staining to assess cortex contact.

Agreement on claims C18-C21. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the differential effects on cytoplasmic versus cortical actin supported by fluorescence intensity measurements. No specific methodological concerns were raised by peer reviewers about these findings.

Partial disagreement on claims C22-C26. OpenEval finds the co-IP and protein expression data supported but notes unexplained mechanisms. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about whether the immunoprecipitation results reflect meiotic oocytes specifically, since experiments used whole ovary containing both somatic cells and oocytes.

Disagreement on claims C27-C33. OpenEval finds the FMNL2-INF2 interaction and ER distribution data well-supported across multiple approaches. Peer reviewers find the ER analysis unconvincing, noting it relies on subjective assessment of clustering and lacks objective parameters and timing information.

Disagreement on claims C34-C41. OpenEval finds the mitochondrial defects comprehensively supported by distribution patterns, JC-1 staining, and rescue experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly find the mitochondria distribution analysis unconvincing, citing subjective assessment of clustering and missing objective parameters and timing.

Partial overlap on claims C60-C64. OpenEval finds these summary conclusions well-supported by collective evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting several conclusions are overstated and the main findings are not fully convincing, particularly given concerns about underlying data (ER/mitochondria analysis, IP specificity, spindle migration quantification).

Partial overlap on claims C67, C74, C82, C94, C95. OpenEval appropriately categorizes these as uncertain speculative mechanistic interpretations requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty about mechanistic conclusions, noting overstatement and lack of conviction about main findings, consistent with OpenEval's assessment that these require direct experimental validation.

OpenEval evaluated claims C42-C101 as background knowledge and literature citations appropriately supported by prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation was found for these contextual and citation claims.
